question: What tragic incident happened in the life of Robert Clive in 1774?

options.text: He was given death penalty on the charges of corruption

solution:
The correct answer is __**He committed suicide.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Robert Clive**, also known as **Clive of India**, played a key role in establishing British control over India during the 18th century. However, his later life was marked by controversies and personal struggles. 
• In **1774**, Robert Clive died by **suicide**. He was found to have used a penknife to end his life at the age of **49**. 
• Clive suffered from **health issues**, including chronic pain due to gallstones, and was known to take opium for relief, which likely contributed to his mental health struggles. 
• His life was also marred by accusations of **corruption** and **mismanagement** during his tenure in India. He faced severe criticism in Britain after returning from India, which may have exacerbated his emotional and psychological distress. 
• While his achievements in India were significant, including the victory at the **Battle of Plassey (1757)**, his later years were overshadowed by personal and professional challenges. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Early Life and Career:** 
• Robert Clive was born in **1725** in England and joined the **British East India Company** as a clerk in **1744**. 
• He played a pivotal role in consolidating British power in India, especially with his victory at the **Battle of Plassey**, which marked the beginning of British dominance in Bengal. 
• **Controversies and Corruption:** 
• Clive faced accusations of **embezzlement** and misuse of power during his time in India. 
• He was summoned by the British Parliament in **1772** to defend his actions, and although he was ultimately exonerated, the scrutiny took a toll on his reputation and mental health. 
• **Health Issues:** 
• Clive struggled with **physical ailments**, including gallstones, and his dependence on opium for pain relief likely worsened his psychological state. 
• Mental health support and understanding during the 18th century were limited, leaving him vulnerable to emotional distress. 
• **Legacy:** 
• Despite his tragic end, Clive is remembered as a key architect of British imperialism in India, laying the foundation for nearly two centuries of British rule. 
• His contributions remain a subject of debate, with critics highlighting his role in exploiting India, while others focus on his military and administrative accomplishments. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Battle of Plassey (1757):** This battle marked the beginning of British control over Bengal and eventually much of India. Clive's victory over Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah was a turning point in Indian history. 
• **Dual Administration:** Clive introduced the system of dual administration in Bengal, where the British controlled revenue collection while the Nawab retained nominal authority. 
• **Parliamentary Inquiry:** Clive faced intense scrutiny in the British Parliament, leading to significant stress and a tarnished public image, despite his acquittal. 
• **Influence on British Imperialism:** Clive's policies and victories laid the groundwork for the expansion of British influence in India, making him a pivotal figure in colonial history. </ul
